newsitem.title: UK: Meyer sees no impact from upturn until 1997.
newsitem.headline: Meyer sees no impact from upturn until 1997.

text.p: Timber and building products group Meyer International Plc said on Wednesday there were signs of improvement in its key markets, but it was unlikely this would make an impact on the company's results until next year.

Chairman Harry Langman said in a statement with the group's first half results that "Softwood prices continue to recover and the improvement in housing starts and transactions should lead to increased demand for both timber and building materials."
He said actions taken by the group would help it to benefit from any upswing in demand.

Meyer said profits at its Jewson division, which is being restructured, were hit by a subdued UK market for repair, maintenance and improvement. Meyer said this market historically lagged the housing market by several months.
Its forest products business improved, reflecting an increase in timber prices.
Meyer's shares were four pence lower at 383.5 by 0909 GMT. --London Newsroom +44 71 542 7717
